chapter: Silvers, Rampart Street and Army service
title: Drafted in 1942 and kept in the States by special services
summary: Drafted into the 92nd Division infantry at Fort McClellan, he trained soldiers and, because he could read a map, was kept from combat in special services.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: so when did you join the Air Force when you go to S.E.S.A. Air Force
went to Army in 1942 got out in 1945 I stayed in Army three years and a few months and a few days and

were you stationed you I first went into the Army in 1942 I was drafted right here at Fort Jackson right here in central Louisiana not not not camp no well I got discharged from camp Polk but anyway I was trained at Fort McClellan Alabama in the infantry with the 92nd Division which is one of the largest and one of the most professional group of black soldiers ever put together by United States only who were segregated but we were big time soldiers you see and that was the infantry having good legs and having a college background I could read well I became a corporal and the war started getting hot and I started training soldiers to go overseas I sent soldiers to Fort Manning Fort Sill Oklahoma I sent them all across the country and it was I think it was Captain Knox

called to me one day, said look, we need your craftsmanship, you're training all these soldiers to go overseas, but I'm going to keep you here. I said, but look, these are my soldiers, Captain, I'm training. No, you got to stay here, we got to put you in special services. I said, what is that? What is that? You said, well, see, we're getting a lot of black soldiers and white soldiers who can't read or write none too well, and ever since those soldiers got lost out there in the hills of Alabama that night when it was raining, you were the only one before you became a sergeant, could read a map, even my first sergeant couldn't read a map. When I found out you were talented, I'm making you a member of my non-commissioned staff, and I'm going to keep you in the States, and he wouldn't let me go overseas. So when I found out...
So your ability to read and write well kept you from combat.
